senses.definition: To be insensitive, insolent, or rude to (somebody); to affront or demean (someone).
senses.example:
- Marvel owns your gods!
- Insulting is not arguing.

senses.definition: To assail, assault, or attack; (specifically, military) to carry out an assault, attack, or onset without preparation.
senses.example:
Giue me thy knife, I will inſult on him,
 Flattering my ſelfes, as if it were the Moore,
 Come hither purpoſely to poyſon me.

senses.definition: To behave in an obnoxious and superior manner (against or over someone).
senses.example: And doe you ſe how he inſulteth ouer me, as though hee had gotten a great aduantage, and how hee taketh heere his reuenge vpon me, for the ſhipwracke hee ſuffered before, in the matter of his ſyllogyſme?
So looks the pent-vp Lyon o're the Wretch, / That trembles vnder his deuouring Pawes: / And ſo he walkes, inſulting o're his Prey, / And ſo he comes, to rend his Limbes aſunder.

senses.definition: Action or form of speech deliberately intended to be rude; (countable) a particular act or statement having this effect.
wordFamily: an insult to one is an insult to all

senses.definition: Something that causes offence (for example, by being of an unacceptable quality).
senses.example: The way the orchestra performed tonight was an insult to my ears.
wordFamily: an insult to one is an insult to all

senses.definition: Something causing disease or injury to the body or bodily processes; the injury so caused.
senses.example: The exact nature of the teratological insult in diabetic pregnancy, and the cell biological details of the induced disturbances, are not known.
wordFamily: an insult to one is an insult to all

senses.definition: An assault or attack; (specifically, military, obsolete) an assault, attack, or onset carried out without preparation.
senses.example: Then fir'd with pious Rage, the gen'rous Train / Run madly forward, to revenge the ſlain. / And ſome with eager haſte their Jav'lins throw; / And ſome, with Sword in hand, aſſault the Foe. / The wiſh'd Inſult the Latine Troops embrace; / And meet their Ardour in the middle Space.

senses.example: The Bull's Inſult at Four ſhe [the mother cow] may ſuſtain; / But, after Ten, from Nuptial Rites refrain. / Six Seaſons uſe; but then releaſe the Cow, / Unfit for Love, and for the lab'ring Plough.
